summary: 1949 Missouri Department of Conservation 100-foot Aermotor fire tower near Mountain View, Howell County; MDC still uses it to spot wildfires; NHLR-registered 2013.

access.note: The 26.8-acre grounds are open to the public, but the tower is a working MDC lookout. No source read says the public may climb it.

visit.trail_note: From Mountain View: Highway 60 west 1.5 miles, County Road 2990 north 0.5 mile, then County Road 3400 west 0.25 mile to the towersite grounds.

events.note: Towersite acquired in fiscal 1947-48: 80 acres, per Commission annual report
Built by the Missouri Department of Conservation in 1949, per the register
A Commission towerman lived at the tower with his family, per a May 1959 newspaper report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Late-1940s state records give the towersite as 80 acres; MDC's current towersite page gives 26.8 acres. The sources do not say when or why the acreage changed, so the story reports both figures.

notes_for_editor: Built 1949 matches the register; the 1947-48 land acquisition precedes it and is consistent. The register's "100' Aermotor" does not say whether the height is to the cab floor, so height_m 30.5 is the stated tower height and the editor should confirm. Status and staffing rest on MDC's towersite page, which is undated but describes the tower in present tense as used by MDC staff to spot wildfires. The 1959 towerman death is in the story without his name; the JSON quotes avoid the name too. The acreage difference (80 acres in the late 1940s, 26.8 acres now) is unexplained. A web search summary tied the 1949 date to a different tower in a Missouri Life article; it was not used. No photos added.
